content.title: Reuse Without Abstraction Debt
goals: Recognize when reuse justifies an abstraction and when premature generalization makes a component harder to understand.

content.title: What is abstraction debt?
content.text:
Abstraction debt appears when an abstraction creates more coordination and special cases than the duplication would have created.

You now have to understand the abstraction before changing either use.

content.question:
Two components share the same outer panel structure but have completely different inner content.

Which is often the simpler design?

options.text: Force both into one highly configurable mega-component.
Share the stable outer shell and compose each inner content separately.

feedback.correct: Reuse the stable boundary and keep variable behavior in composition. Do not abstract every difference into a prop.
feedback.incorrect: Reuse the stable boundary and keep variable behavior in composition. Do not abstract every difference into a prop.

content.title: Good duplication vs bad duplication
content.text:
Some repeated code can be acceptable when:

- the concepts are likely to change independently,
- the repeated code is tiny and obvious,
- an abstraction would require many conditionals,
- the shared behavior is not actually stable.

The goal is not zero duplication.

The goal is **low accidental coupling**.

content.question: You have copied the same three-line label pattern in two components.

options.text: Extract it immediately into `UniversalLabelSystem` with seven props.
Leave it alone until a shared requirement actually emerges.

feedback.correct: A tiny duplication with no stable shared behavior may be cheaper than a premature abstraction.
feedback.incorrect: A tiny duplication with no stable shared behavior may be cheaper than a premature abstraction.

content.title: A stronger reason to abstract

content.question: Which sentence is closer to senior reasoning?

options.text: “Abstract when the shared concept is real and stable enough that one boundary reduces future cost.”

feedback.correct: Reuse is a means to reduce change cost, not a scoreboard.
feedback.incorrect: Reuse is a means to reduce change cost, not a scoreboard.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** The best abstraction removes repeated decisions, not merely repeated lines.
**Senior habit:** Before extracting a component, ask whether the places using it are likely to change together.
nextSteps: Look at one repeated UI pattern and argue for either abstraction or intentional duplication.
